question: Which article of the Indian Constitution deals with sessions of Parliament?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Article 85**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Article 85** of the **Indian Constitution** deals with the sessions of Parliament, prorogation, and dissolution.
 
• The **President** has the authority to summon each House of Parliament at such intervals that there should not be a gap of more than **six months** between two sessions.
 
• Under this Article, the President can also **prorogue** a session or **dissolve** the Lok Sabha.
 
• The Constitution ensures that Parliament meets regularly to fulfill its legislative functions and oversight responsibilities effectively.
 
• This provision is crucial to prevent excessive delays in legislative work and to maintain the functioning of a democratic government.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Article 74**:

 
 
• This Article mandates the existence of a **Council of Ministers** with the **Prime Minister** at its head to aid and advise the President in exercising his functions.
 
• It emphasizes the role of the executive in the Indian parliamentary system.
 
 
 
• **Article 93**:
 
 
• This Article pertains to the **Speaker** and **Deputy Speaker** of the Lok Sabha.
 
• It requires that the House of the People elect its Speaker and Deputy Speaker as soon as possible after the first meeting.
 
 
 
• **Article 100**:
 
 
• This Article deals with the **voting procedures** in Parliament, including the requirement for a quorum.
 
• A quorum is the minimum number of members required to conduct parliamentary proceedings, which is **one-tenth** of the total membership of the House.
 
 
 
• **Sessions of Parliament:**
 
 
• India's Parliament typically has three sessions a year: the **Budget Session** (February to May), the **Monsoon Session** (July to September), and the **Winter Session** (November to December).
 
• The **President** summons and prorogues parliamentary sessions under Article 85.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Prorogation vs. Dissolution:**

 
 
• **Prorogation** refers to the termination of a session of Parliament by the President, without dissolving it.
 
• **Dissolution**, on the other hand, applies only to the Lok Sabha and leads to its reconstitution through general elections.
 
 
 
• **Parliamentary Sessions:**
 
 
• The interval between two sessions cannot exceed six months, ensuring that Parliament meets at least twice a year.
 
• This provision safeguards the legislative process and oversight mechanisms essential for democratic governance.
 
 
 
• **Historical Context:**
 
 
• Article 85 reflects the influence of the British parliamentary system, where similar provisions exist for summoning and proroguing sessions.
 
• It is vital for maintaining the balance of power between the executive and legislative branches in India.
